note: MemScope (arXiv 2610.21170v1, 2026-10-15, preprint). Headline numbers on screen: 63% and 87%, GAIA diagnostic ablation (Table 5, sec 4.4), the authors' own runs, one number per setting, no spread reported; backbone model not stated for Table 5. 87% is the Trace + Memory Inspection variant, not the full MemScope system (Patch History variant: 83.33%). The protagonist case (Table 6, App. B.1) comes from the Trace-only variant; its cause is 'proposed' and its outcome is not reported. Code and memory state both vary across compared runs (Fig 3 caption). Round 2: the hook no longer states the cause as fact; the protagonist case is told as the paper records it (zero-step run, no notes reached the agent); 87% is labelled as one test setting (the best of the six in Table 5) and the full MemScope 83% is spoken.

numbers.0: Zero steps in the recorded GAIA case: trajectory_length=0, zero-length traces, "two zero-step failures" (Table 6, p. 9; App. B.1, p. 18). On screen as "0 steps".
numbers.6: Table 6 (p. 9), the recorded GAIA repair case; tag 'recorded case, Table 6'.
numbers.63: GAIA diagnostic ablation, Summary-only row: 63.33% task accuracy (Table 5, p. 8; sec 4.4). Patch Agent received only grouped failure reports.
numbers.83: Full MemScope (with Patch History) on the GAIA diagnostic ablation: 83.33% (Table 5, sec 4.4). Spoken as "Full MemScope: eighty three".
numbers.87: GAIA diagnostic ablation, Trace + Memory Inspection row: 86.67% task accuracy (Table 5, p. 8; sec 4.4). Patch Agent read raw traces and could inspect the memory store. Not the full MemScope score.
numbers.83.33: MemScope with Patch History on the same ablation (Table 5, sec 4.4); caption only.
numbers.4.4: Section number (sec 4.4); also the median code-change ratio (4.4%) across the archived provider transitions; separately, the median transition touches one function (sec 4.4, p. 9; abstract). Post text only.
numbers.2610.21170: arXiv id in the closing credit

evidence_incidental.1: R1 crop (p. 5, line 'provider code through the read-only tools in Table 1 ...'): the table number 'Table 1'; also 'Listing 1' above R2 if the crop shows it.

claims.l01: Hook. Sec 1 and App. B.1: a recorded GAIA failure in the memory architecture (missing guidance, zero-step runs). "Fix one line, or rewrite it all?" is a question: MemScope makes localized edits (sec 3.3); prior architecture-level methods "propose complete executable architectures" (Fig 1 caption) and are "often leading to large-scale rewrites" (abstract). No cause is stated as fact.
claims.l02: Sec 1, Fig 1: MemScope applies 'a localized, in-place edit to the existing provider'; 'only the highlighted code region is modified'.
claims.l03: Sec 4.1 and sec 3: the Agent Executor (Flash-Searcher) performs GAIA/xBench web research tasks and stores distilled memory items (Eq. 3-4).
claims.l04: Sec 1: the memory architecture is 'the executable logic for storage, retrieval, and presentation' / 'the code that determines what is stored, how it is retrieved'.
claims.l05: Table 6 / App. B.1: Trace-only inspects trajectory_length=0 and empty memory_guidance_steps; B.1 "two zero-step failures". "The memory gives the agent no notes" = empty memory guidance ("missing guidance", B.1). "Fails": the case is one of the recorded GAIA failures. No search outcome or answer is claimed.
claims.l06: "Usually" mirrors the abstract's "typically". Abstract: recent self-evolving approaches use "execution feedback, typically represented as evaluation scores or compressed summaries". Sec 3.3 (p. 5): "A score alone cannot distinguish absent experience, filtering/ranking errors, and ineffective guidance formatting". Receipt R1.
claims.l07: Abstract: "Without a precise failure location, existing approaches lack a clear code-level target for modification ... often leading to large-scale rewrites of an otherwise capable memory architecture." No rewrite baseline row is implied.
claims.l08: Sec 3.3: the Patch Agent produces 'a localized code update' with exact old-to-new replacements; prompts 'prohibit broad rewrites'.
claims.l09: Sec 3.3, Table 1: the Patch Agent inspects raw execution traces. Table 6 / App. B.1: zero-length traces (trajectory_length=0) and empty memory_guidance_steps: zero steps, no notes.
claims.l10: App. B.1 (p. 18): "a specific retrieval-code change"; Trace-only "identifies an early return under MemoryStatus.IN as the proposed cause of missing guidance". Table 6: "Early-return guard under MemoryStatus.IN may suppress guidance". "May" keeps the hedge, and the on-screen tag reads "proposed cause" (B.1); "search code" = retrieval code; "stop the search too soon" = early return.
claims.l11: App. A.1, Listing 1 (p. 15): "Your job is to make one minimal, evidence-backed patch to the CURRENT provider." Receipt R2. Table 6 / B.1: "Remove the early-return guard" / "removes that guard". The outcome of this case is not reported and not claimed.
claims.l12: Sec 4.4 / Table 5: the authors vary the diagnostic inputs of the Patch Agent on the same GAIA tasks. Summary-only ("receives candidate reports", Evidence = Summary): 63.33%. This is the authors' own ablation, not an older method.
claims.l13: Table 5, sec 4.4: Trace + Memory Inspection (raw trace plus the memory store): 86.67%, "the highest GAIA diagnostic accuracy" of the six settings. Full MemScope (adds Patch History): 83.33%. On screen 87% is labelled as one test setting and 83% as full MemScope.
claims.l14: Small test: sec 4.4 calls the 86.67 vs 83.33 gap "the one-task difference" (about 30 tasks); one number per setting, no spread reported. Authors' own runs. Closing line summarizes the method; no new claim.
